text:
sam: heads up — saw a weird case in Console where the project sidebar shows rows belonging to a different project after I rapidly switch projects. small repro in staging, happened twice in a 5m window. cc @maria :eyes:

maria: ugh. can you drop the repro steps and a screenshot? which flow — quick switch dropdown or url param?

sam: quick dropdown. steps: open project A -> open insights panel -> switch to project B quickly -> panel still renders some A rows. screenshot attached. no full page reload.

chris: possible caching / context race. quick question: are you on the new project-resolver middleware? we changed the prefetch ordering last week.

sam: yep, latest canary. repro curl of what the panel calls: ```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" 
  -H "X-Project-Id: B" 
  "https://staging.console.internal/api/insights?panel=recent"``` but the backend sometimes returns rows for A.

elaine: if it's intermittent it smells like a per-request context getting mutated across concurrent handlers. saw similar in a downstream service (not console) where we reused a shared object for request state.

maria: i'm looking at logs for the panel requests. interesting: when switch happens fast, the route call hits project-resolver which does: read cookie lastSeenProject, then fallback to header. if header missing it writes lastSeenProject = currentProject after auth. that could cause a write of A into the cookie in the middle of processing B's request.

chris: yep — middleware order matters. prefetch fetches using req.context.project, but auth middleware sets lastSeenProject after the resolver in some rollout pods. race: request B arrives, auth sets cookie from previous request A, then resolver picks up that stale cookie for B.

sam: that matches what i saw. any quick mitigations? we need to stop cross-request writes until the resolver is stable.

maria: quick patch i can try: make project-resolver idempotent and avoid writing lastSeenProject during the request lifecycle — only set it on explicit user navigation (client side) or on a dedicated endpoint. patch idea: ```js
// in project-resolver.js
if (!req.headers['x-project-id']) {
  // don't mutate cookie during normal API path to avoid overwriting concurrent requests
  // preserve existing lastSeenProject for reads only
  req.context.project = req.cookies.lastSeenProject || DEFAULT_PROJECT;
} else {
  req.context.project = req.headers['x-project-id'];
}
```

elaine: canary note: we rolled the resolver change to 20% last week. that rollout shard probably has the mismatched middleware order. i'd rollback the resolver change in the shard and run the reproducer. i'll take it. :+1:

chris: also add a quick guard in the shared request-store: ensure we don't reuse the same object reference across concurrent requests. `Object.assign({}, baseCtx)` or use a factory per req. small hotspot but helpful.

sam: can you add a telemetry event we can filter on? something like `project_context_unexpected` with tags: expected_project, resolved_project, pod, handler_latency. we can populate a dashboard for the last hour.

maria: yep adding metric now. will push a lightweight counter and a kql for the dashboard. link will be posted here when ready.

dev-bot: deploy started: staging/resolver-patch v2026.3 -> 3 pods. CI: all green.

elaine: i rolled back the canary shard to 0% on the resolver change and repro no longer triggers. confirming that rollback makes it go away.

sam: great — thanks. follow-ups: (1) maria to land the idempotent-resolver patch and add telemetry (2) chris to audit request-store reuse across console services (3) create a small e2e that rapid-switches projects to catch regressions. assigning owners?

maria: i'll open the PR and include tests. pr will include the telemetry tag and a note to QA for the e2e.

chris: i'll do the request-store audit and open issues where reuse is found.

elaine: i'll write a tiny puppeteer script to run the rapid-switch e2e and add it to the canary gate.

sam: thanks all. cc @oncall if we see production spikes. i'll keep an eye on the telemetry once the counter is live. :wave:
